<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-melon" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-melon-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of melon, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

Melon, as sold; As sold, as eaten or fresh weight, µg/kg; no moisture conversion. Distribution of subgroup median concentration values.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Reference (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Q1</th><th scope="col">Median</th><th scope="col">Q3</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Primary HMI reference</td><td>≤3</td><td>≤5</td><td>1.65–10 (bounded)</td></tr><tr><td>Alternative weighting</td><td>≤3</td><td>≤5</td><td>1.4–9.5 (bounded)</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>67 reference units; 1 sampling family. Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>WHO GEMS/Food</td><td>67</td><td>100%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians for melon, as sold on a as sold, as eaten or fresh weight basis: monitoring results summarized as one median per reporting region, sampling type and collection year, total diet composites and printed sample values as single observations, and printed subgroup medians from ordinary farms or markets. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>WHO GEMS/Food is the only compatible sampling family for melon, as sold on this basis in the completed melon ledger, so this single-family reference cannot represent other markets. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" class="internal" data-slug="sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" data-no-cite-meta>WHO GEMS/Food</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. <summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does processing change heavy metals in melon?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Only comparisons between forms in the same study are available, not before-and-after measurements of the same melon.<sup class="cite">[[sources/nisa2020-quetta-market-fruits-vegetables-metals|10]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Nisa KU, Samiullah, Khan N, Attiq-ur-Rehman · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/nisa2020-quetta-market-fruits-vegetables-metals">Detection of Heavy metals in Fruits and Vegetables available in the Market of Quetta city</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Al-Nahrain Journal of Science 23(1):47-56</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/nisa2020-quetta-market-fruits-vegetables-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Melon, peel or outer layer (local market) had lead lower at 275 µg/kg, against 678 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (melon, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/nisa2020-quetta-market-fruits-vegetables-metals|10]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Nisa KU, Samiullah, Khan N, Attiq-ur-Rehman · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/nisa2020-quetta-market-fruits-vegetables-metals">Detection of Heavy metals in Fruits and Vegetables available in the Market of Quetta city</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Al-Nahrain Journal of Science 23(1):47-56</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/nisa2020-quetta-market-fruits-vegetables-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-melon-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-melon-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in melon is inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in melon is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Inorganic arsenic, the more toxic form, was measured in 5 results from 3 sources, far fewer than total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span
